questions.q: Why build your own Betaflight firmware?
options: Flash is limited: only what is needed
So the firmware runs the PID loop faster
No reason, a ready-made one exists
questions.explain: Cloud Build builds for your list of options.

options: The drone's name in the OSD
A USE_* flag outside the lists
A CLI setting with a user-defined name
questions.explain: An option outside the standard lists, a USE_* flag entered without the prefix; it is not tested on all boards, and a pin is assigned through resource.

questions.q: Where can you see the build key on the board?
options: The build_info command in the CLI
questions.explain: The BUILD KEY is printed by `status`; `version` shows the version and the target. Betaflight has no build_info command.
./waf configure --board X; ./waf copter. The target is described in the board's hwdef.dat.

questions.q: What do you lose by removing GPS from ArduPilot firmware?
options: Only the OSD elements with coordinates and speed
questions.explain: For good, not just for now. The decision is sensible if you understand the consequences.

questions.q: Can you paste a diff all from another major version into your own build?
options: Only in dump format and only on F7 boards
No, just as for a standard one
Yes, if the build has the same target
questions.explain: A custom build + a config from another version = unpredictability.

questions.q: What do you check right after flashing your own build?
options: That version and the BUILD KEY match, the gyro and the ports
Only the color of the LEDs
Nothing: the build is guaranteed to be correct
questions.explain: Check the build against the expected one and re-read what is critical: gyro, ports, receiver.

questions.q: How do you name your build so that it can be reproduced?
options: With the date and the commit hash
questions.explain: The date and the commit hash state unambiguously what it was built from.
